children: Egypt’s Ministry of Finance plans to offer 16 water desalination, wastewater treatment and electricity projects worth a combined $3.08 billion under the public-private partnership (PPP) model, according to a government document seen by local Arabic language financial daily Al Borsa News.
Desalination accounts for the largest investments in the planned portfolio, including a $1 billion seawater desalination plant in Suez Governorate and an $800 million plant in Port Said Governorate.
The two projects will have a combined production capacity of 1 million cubic metres per day (m3/day), to be developed in two phases.

The Alamein desalination plant and Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE) desalination plant have reached the final tendering stage, while the Port Said and Suez projects are currently being offered, the report said.
The Alamein project is valued at $170 million, while the SCZONE desalination plant in Ain Sokhna is estimated at $710 million.
The PPP pipeline also includes a $150 million sludge treatment plant at Abu Rawash and a $23.5 million reverse-wash water recycling project at the Mostorod Water Plant.
Four industrial wastewater treatment projects are planned at Amreya in Alexandria ($40 million), Abu Rawash ($48 million), Port Said ($65 million) and Wadi El Natrun ($24 million).

Electricity projects include substations and networks in several new and industrial cities. They comprise a $10 million developers' station and networks project and a $21 million station serving the Eighth Industrial Zone in Sadat City; a $4 million station in 6th of October City's Ayat area; and electricity distribution networks in New Mansoura City and New Aswan City, valued at $12 million and $2 million, respectively.
(Writing by Majda Muhsen; Editing by Anoop Menon)
